title: Lazy field widgets remember a failed first chunk load and never recover without a page reload (date/datetime/rich text editors, rich text display, filter condition cell, image crop, getLazyFieldWidget cache)
body:
repo:objectstack#2 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmRY38EZf38Yy3zthbY

Family card filed by the seat from the #36451 dev (PR #36607, which fixes the line-item grid with `GridFieldOnceLoaded`). Not claimed. Related: #36451.

Suggested-grade: p2
Suggested-domain: `domain:ui`

## What happens

A `React.lazy` component caches its first import promise. When the chunk load fails once (a deploy that replaced the chunk, a dropped connection), every later render reuses the rejected promise, so the widget stays broken until the page is reloaded. #36451 fixed this for the lazy line-item grid only.

## Where (the whole family; each a pin)

- `FieldEditWidget`: date, datetime and rich text editors
- `richTextDisplay`
- `FilterConditionCell`
- the image field's crop dialog
- `getLazyFieldWidget` in the fields package's `index.tsx`, which caches one lazy component per field type

Measured by the dev: date, markdown, filter condition and `getLazyFieldWidget('date')`. The rest are read from the code.

## Ask

Apply #36607's approach (a once-loaded wrapper that drops a rejected import so the next render retries) to every site above, through one shared helper rather than a copy per site. A test per site pins that a first failed load followed by a successful one renders the widget without a reload.

## Re-check

`git grep -n "React.lazy\|lazy(" ui/packages/fields/src` lists the sites; each one goes through the shared helper when this is fixed.
